question: Over the ten years to 2023, US funds returned 7.3% a year, but the people invested in them earned 6.3%. Where did the point go?
answer: Into timing. A fund's return assumes money sat still for ten years. Investors' money arrived after good runs and left after bad ones, so more of it was in for the falls. Same funds, same fees, same tax: the missing point is behaviour, roughly 15% of what the funds earned.
move: Ask whose average a figure is: the product's or the people's.
ask: When did I last buy something because it had just gone up?

clues.text: The gap is about one point a year, every year, for a decade.
The funds' 7.3% is already counted after their fees.
Both figures are before tax, so tax cannot open a gap between them.
Money poured in after rises and fled after falls.

scene.why: Fees and tax hit both numbers alike. Only one thing differs: when people's money was in.
